claims.claim: (a) The Phase 3 (2024, 223 windows, 81.2%) and Phase 4 (2020, 223 windows, 12.1%) prompts sent to the LLM in Nov 2025 carried calendar dates, contradicting the papers' statement that dates are mapped to relative labels. All 446 prompts carry dates.
claims.evidence:
Batch metadata (batch_jobs/batch_batch_<id>_metadata.json) links batch_691ea7f7b79481909f4667eaff640f26 ('Paper #2 Phase 3: Full 2024 baseline validation (223 windows)') to input_file phase3_full_2024_baseline_v2.jsonl. It links batch_691f37d94ef0819099136e88a69bef82 ('Phase 4: 2020 baseline (0DTE hypothesis)') to batch_regime_20251120_104630.jsonl. Both files are present in reports/validation/paper2_regime_windows/batch_jobs/. File mtimes are consistent with the batch creation times. phase3_full_2024_baseline.jsonl is byte-identical to v2 (same md5 900eb103...). The result YAMLs name the same batch ids. results_batch_<id>.jsonl custom_ids match the input custom_ids exactly (223/223 each). I parsed both inputs with python and a regex. Phase 3: 223/223 prompts contain an ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, with exactly 30 per prompt (min 30, max 30), and 223/223 contain a 4-digit year. Phase 4: also 223/223 prompts with exactly 30 ISO dates and a 4-digit year. Neither file has any 'Day T-k' label (regex 'Day T[+-]\d+' gives 0/223 in each). Every request is a single user message to o4-mini. Window 1 of Phase 3 (custom_id window-2024-02-13) reads '## 30-DAY GEX DATA

2024-01-02: -33.01B
2024-01-03: -33.27B ... 2024-02-13: -41.08B'. Window 1 of Phase 4 (window-2020-02-13) reads '2020-01-02: +8.91B ... 2020-02-13: +7.51B'. The prompt body has no month names and no ticker symbols (SPY, QQQ, IWM and S&P all 0/223 in both files), so the dates are the only identifier. The model actually used the dates: the Phase 3 response for the window ending 2024-06-05 quotes 'pos->neg on 2024-06-05' and '2024-06-04'. The yaml reasoning field for Phase 3 and Phase 4 windows, searched for ISO dates, finds 1 quoting window in Phase 3 and 0 in Phase 4; the raw results JSONL contains the 2024-06-04 string.
claims.correction: The papers' statement that Phase 3 and Phase 4 prompts used 'Day T-29 ... Day T+0' labels is false for these two runs. State it as follows: Phases 1 and 2 (Nov 2025, Day T-k labels) and the later multi-year runs (2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 in Nov 2025, and Phase 4A/5 in Jan 2026) were relabelled. The 2024 full-year run (Phase 3) and the 2020 baseline (Phase 4) were run with calendar dates visible (YYYY-MM-DD, 30 per prompt), and no ticker. Also correct the figure and appendix descriptions of the prompt (JRFM 07_Appendix_A_Prompts.tex ~line 73 says the placeholder is filled with 'Day T-29: +3.42B' format).

claims.claim: (a, side check) Cause and code path of the dated files; Phase 1, 2, 4A/5 prompts are labelled Day T-k.
claims.evidence: I scanned every JSONL in batch_jobs. Day-T labelled and containing zero ISO dates: Phase 1 (batch_regime_20251106_184057, 54 windows 2024-01-02..2024-03-27; and the 20251119_2217/2222/2228 reruns); the Phase 2 controls for 2024Q1 and 2020 (20251119_2306xx files, 223 windows each, Day T); the Nov-22 multi-year files (2021, 2022, 2023, 2025: 221-251 windows each, Day T); and phase4a_postgresql_20260104_*.jsonl (1476 windows, Day T). Only the two baseline files, phase3_full_2024_baseline(_v2).jsonl and batch_regime_20251120_104630.jsonl, have dates (223/223 each). Note that the 'batch_regime_20251119_230659/230714/230718' 2020 files are Phase 2 shuffle/transitional/low-magnitude controls, not the Phase 4 baseline. The code builds the table verbatim from day['date'] (src/llm/mechanics_prompt_builder.py build_regime_prompt: 'date_label = day["date"]  # Already obfuscated'). prepare_batch_file in src/validation/batch_regime_validator.py passes end_date for custom_id only. scripts/validation/paper2/05_validate_regime_windows_batch.py (lines 163-176) replaces each date with 'Day T{offset}' before building the prompt, as does 04_validate_regime_windows.py (_obfuscate_sequence). The current committed code therefore would produce Day T labels. I could not find the script that generated the two dated files; the repo has no script or git commit mentioning phase3_full_2024_baseline (git log -S gives only the merge 477bb41, and the only code reference is a docs line citing a nonexistent 'input_phase3_full_2024_baseline.jsonl'). It is SPECULATION that the Nov 20 Phase 3/4 files were built by an ad-hoc script or notebook that bypassed the obfuscation step (the Phase 3 file mtime 05:04-05:08 UTC and Phase 4 file mtime 15:22 UTC on Nov 20, with filename 104630 local).
claims.correction: Do not say the pipeline always obfuscated. Say: the obfuscation code path exists in 04/05 scripts, but the Phase 3 and 4 input files were not produced by it, and the generating script is not preserved in the repository.

claims.claim: (b) The Phase 3/4 headline contrast (81.2% vs 12.1%, 69.1 pp, phi 0.672/0.69) therefore rests on dated prompts.
claims.evidence: The numbers do rest on the dated runs: phase3_baseline_2024_full_year.yaml has regimes_detected 181 / total 223 = 81.166% (batch_691ea7f7...), phase4_baseline_2020.yaml has 27 / 223 = 12.108% (batch_691f37d9...), and the differences are 69.06 pp. I recomputed phi from the 2x2 table [[181,42],[27,196]] and got 0.6922, Fisher exact p = 1.82e-52. That matches JRFM's phi = 0.69 and p = 1.8e-52. The AIAI abstract's phi = 0.672 does NOT reproduce from 181/223 vs 27/223 (I could not identify its source; SPECULATION: a different cell split or counting). Independently parsing results JSONL with a simple JSON regex gave 169/207 and 27/219 because 16 and 4 responses failed to parse; the YAML counts 181 and 27, so the published count includes responses repaired or re-parsed by the pipeline. I could not test whether dates change the outcome: no Day-T version of the Nov 2025 2024 full-year or 2020 baseline run exists locally (the Day-T 2020 files are shuffled/transitional/low-magnitude controls, and the Phase 4A/5 Day-T runs of Jan 2026 are a different input - call-only GEX per the upstream finding). So the causal effect of dates on the 81.2 vs 12.1 contrast is unknown. The dated prompts also had no spot or DTE fields: the prompt contains only date: net GEX in billions, contradicting AIAI 03_Methodology.tex:33 ('receives GEX magnitudes, spot prices, and days to expiration').
claims.correction: Report that the 81.2% / 12.1% contrast (181/223 vs 27/223; phi = 0.692 from these counts, so AIAI's 0.672 needs checking or correcting) was obtained with calendar-dated prompts (30 YYYY-MM-DD dates per prompt, no ticker), so it is not an obfuscated result and cannot support the memorization-control claim. The obfuscation claim holds only for Phase 1, Phase 2 controls, and the multi-year/Phase 4A/5 runs. Either rerun Phase 3 and 4 with Day T-k labels (a ~$1-2 batch at o4-mini) or reword the Methods/abstract to say that the two baseline years were run with dates visible, and drop 'temporal obfuscation' as the explanation for the headline contrast. Also correct the claim that the LLM receives spot prices and DTE (it received only daily net GEX).

claims.claim: (a) Phase 3 2024 daily series = gex_database.db total_gex, which is -(call+put) excluding 0DTE and therefore negative on every day by construction; 242 real rows + 10 placeholder rows (call/put components 0, no option count, spot 6-7.5% below SPY); every one of the 42 rejected windows contains 3-6 placeholders.
claims.evidence: Reproduced. (1) phase3_full_2024_baseline_v2.jsonl: 223 windows x 30 dated lines; 252 unique dates; every value matches daily_gex_metrics.total_gex (SPY, 2024, 252 rows, created 2025-10-11..11-03) to within 0.005B. (2) DB columns: net_call_gex<0 and net_put_gex<0 on 242 rows, and total_gex = net_call_gex+net_put_gex exactly (ratio 1.0000, i.e. a sum of two NEGATIVE-stored components). (3) Against raw gex.options_chains_partitioned (SPY, gamma*OI*100*S^2*0.01, unsigned gamma, per-date sums for all 2024): total_gex on the 242 real rows equals -(call_ex0DTE + put_ex0DTE): median rel. error 0.31%, p90 1.1%, 242/242 within 5%, corr 0.9989. Full gross incl. 0DTE fits worse (median 16.3%, 2/242 within 5%). Spot checks: 2024-01-02 raw call_ex 16.21 + put_ex 16.60 = 32.81 vs DB -33.01; 2024-03-15 12.65+17.15 = 29.80 vs -29.84. (4) Placeholders (net_call_gex = net_put_gex = 0, options_count NULL, total_gex POSITIVE +10.61..+13.76B): 2024-02-02, 02-09, 02-16, 02-23, 03-01, 03-08, 03-22, 03-28, 06-04, 06-06. All ten were inserted in one burst on 2025-11-03 15:32-15:33 (about 2.7 s apart; rest of year created 2025-10-11/10-16, build_metadata shows an Oct-11 build of 198 rows). Their spot_price is 461-495 (round numbers, e.g. 461.0, 467.0, 482.75) vs the SPY spot 494.35-534.66 in gex.options_daily_summary: gap -6.11% to -7.45% (real rows -0.52% to +0.85%). No .cache/gex_data/SPY/<date> folder exists for these 10 dates. (5) Window-level counts: of 223x30 = 6,690 values sent to the LLM, 6,399 are negative and 291 positive (all 291 are placeholder values); by date 242 negative, 10 positive. (6) The 42 rejected windows (all 'transitional', window ends 2024-02-20..2024-04-18) contain 3 (7 windows), 4 (10), 5 (16) or 6 (9) placeholders, all from the 8 Feb-Mar placeholder dates (0 of the June ones). Detected windows: 130 contain 0 placeholders, 8 contain 1, 41 contain 2, 2 contain 3. Flips: rejected windows 6-12 (all >5), detected 0-5. A re-implementation of the prompt rule (>70% same sign, mean |GEX|>5B, <=5 flips) reproduces the YAML label in 223/223 windows. Replacing the 10 placeholder values by their raw -(ex-0DTE) values (-27.3..-33.3B) turns the rule into 223/223 detected (replacing alone is my replay; dropping them as the F3 inventory says is analogous). (7) Today's gex.options_daily_summary (signed total = call + put, puts negative; matches raw call-put with corr 1.0): 2024 signed net is negative on only 95/252 days and positive on 157; sign agreement with the Phase 3 series on the 242 real days is 38%, corr -0.07; Phase 3 magnitude is about 30B vs a signed mean of 1.26B (gross ex-0DTE about 83% of the gross including 0DTE).
claims.correction: Say: 'the Phase 3 2024 input is the gross (call+put gamma magnitude, same-day expiries excluded) with a negative sign imposed, not a signed net; it is negative on 242 of 252 dates and 6,399 of 6,690 window values, not on every day. The 10 non-negative rows are backfilled placeholder rows (inserted 2025-11-03; zero call/put components, NULL option count, off-market spot), which carry +10.6..+13.8B.' Note the sign was imposed by the formula (the DB stores both components as negative), so the all-negative result is by construction; 'sign-stripped' is the wrong label for 2024 (it is sign-forced; it is the 2020 series that is sign-stripped). The 42 rejections are 100% attributable to the 8 Feb-Mar placeholder rows (7+10+16+9 windows with 3/4/5/6 of them); with the placeholders neutralised the 2024 rate is 223/223, so the 81.2% headline and the 'Feb-Mar volatility' explanation are artifacts of 10 bad rows. The JRFM/AIAI line 'framework correctly rejected 42 windows exhibiting Feb-Mar volatility (6-10 flips)' should be withdrawn (flips are actually 6-12).

claims.claim: (b) The Phase 4 2020 series is positive on 252/252 days although today's signed net is negative on 93 days; it tracks |gex_oi| (r 0.996).
claims.evidence: batch_regime_20251120_104630.jsonl: 223 windows, 252 unique dated values, min +0.01B, max +11.23B, 0 negative, 0 zero, mean 2.853B. Today's signed net for 2020: gex.options_daily_summary total_gex negative on 93/252 days (raw options_chains_partitioned call-put gives the identical 93, corr 1.0). Against .cache/consolidated_historical.db daily_gex_metrics (SPY 2020, 252 rows, gex_oi NULL on 2 dates): corr(phase4, |gex_oi|) = 0.9959 on 250 days; corr(phase4, signed gex_oi) = -0.795; corr(phase4, |total_gex|) = 0.62. Phase 4 vs |gex_oi| is NOT identical: abs diff median 0.06B, p90 0.40B, max 1.21B (exact within 0.006B on only 14 of 250 days; e.g. 2020-01-23 phase4 6.14 vs |gex_oi| 4.93), so the series is an OI-GEX-like magnitude with the sign removed, not literally abs(gex_oi). Also note the stored gex_oi sign is opposite to today's signed net (corr gex_oi vs signed net -0.91; sign agreement 7.6%), and consolidated total_gex is negative on 250/252 days. corr(phase4, today's signed net) = 0.70, corr with |today's net| = 0.81; on the 93 negative-net days phase4 values are 0.01..4.9B (mean 1.40B). Phase 4 YAML: 27/223 detected (12.1%), consistent with a magnitude-only test (a series with no negative values gives persistence 100%, 0 flips in every window).
claims.correction: State that the 2020 comparison series is a magnitude-only (absolute-value, OI-based) series, positive on 252/252 days, whereas the signed net for 2020 is negative on 93/252 days; the 12.1% therefore reflects only the $5B magnitude gate (27 windows >=5B), and 'r = 0.996 with |gex_oi|' should be given as 'high but not exact (median abs. deviation 0.06B, max 1.2B)'. Do not describe it as exactly |gex_oi|.

claims.claim: (c) Hence 'persistent negative' (2024) vs 'positive' (2020) in Table 3 is an artifact of two different sign conventions, not a market feature.
claims.evidence: Follows from (a) and (b): 2024 = gross magnitude forced negative (-(call+put) ex-0DTE); 2020 = absolute-value magnitude, positive. Under one common definition (today's signed net, call-put, from the same raw table) 2024 is positive on 157 and negative on 95 of 252 days (and 2020 positive on 159, negative on 93): neither year is a persistent single-sign regime, and the 2020-vs-2024 sign difference does not appear. Table 3 in both papers (docs/papers/paper2/aiai/04_Results.tex:53 and docs/papers/jrfm/04_Results.tex:119) prints 'Dominant Sign: Negative | Positive | Flip'. Additional corroboration: Phase 1 (same Q1-2024 dates, different file cache) was persistent_positive, and Phase 5 (signed net / call-only series) labels 2024 persistent_positive, so the sign label flips with the input series on the same market dates. Caveat: I did not rerun the LLM; the statement that the sign is not a market feature rests on the series construction and on the deterministic-rule replay (rule == LLM label in 223/223 Phase 3 windows).
claims.correction: Drop the 'Dominant Sign: Negative (2024) vs Positive (2020)' row (and the 'persistent negative regime' narrative in Results/Discussion, fig04_selectivity caption) or restate it as 'sign is set by the input convention (gross forced negative in 2024; absolute value in 2020) and carries no market information'. Any Table 3 persistence comparison (96.0% vs 83.3%; Phase 3 YAML mean persistence 95.65%, Phase 4 persistence 100% in every window) must be recomputed from one consistent signed series.

claims.claim: (a) Paper 1's 242-day scalar GEX series (GEX-assisted arm, 71.5% single-day detection, 'all 242 days negative') is -(call+put) ex-0DTE and therefore negative by construction, so 'persistent negative regime driven by 0DTE' is partly a sign-convention statement.
claims.evidence: reports/validation/paper1_pattern_taxonomy/gamma_positioning_SPY_2024_unbiased.yaml (the same file for stock_pinning and 0dte_hedging): on all 242 days market_metrics.call_gamma < 0 and put_gamma < 0, and call_gamma+put_gamma = net_gex_usd (max relative error 3.5e-16); net < -$2B on 242/242. A sum of two negative terms cannot be positive. I recomputed from .cache/consolidated_historical.db raw_options_chain (72 dates of 2024; GEX = gamma*OI*100*spot^2*0.01 per row): -(call+put) over expirations later than the trade date correlates 0.9967 with the Paper 1 CSV (median relative error 1.6%), while all expirations including 0DTE correlate 0.82 (median error 21%), so the scalar is ex-0DTE. The signed net (calls minus puts, the convention Paper 1 says it uses: src/gex/gex_calculator.py and 04_Experimental_setup.tex:15) does not track the CSV (corr -0.03) and is negative on only 19/72 of those dates (mean +2.7B). Post-rebuild PostgreSQL gex.options_daily_summary (SPY, 2024), joined to the 242 CSV dates, gives 93 negative days, 75 below -$2B and mean +1.26B (all 252 days: 95 negative, mean +1.46B). The pre-rebuild backup table backups.options_daily_summary_pre_rebuild_20261004 is call-only (net_put_gex = 0, positive every day), consistent with the upstream put-dropping bug and not a usable comparison. 71.5% itself reproduces: (168+163+188)/(3*242) = 519/726 = 71.49%. Caveat (analytic, not a data finding): -(call+put) is equivalent to assuming dealers are short every option (customers long all). That is a stated dealer-positioning assumption, and 'signed net' is also an assumption, so the claim is about internal consistency with the paper's own stated convention (calls +, puts -) and not about which sign is true.
claims.correction: Paper 1 should state that its GEX scalar is the negative of the unsigned sum of call and put dollar gamma, excluding same-day expiries, that it equals -(call+put) with both legs negative, and that 'GEX < -$2B on 242/242 days' therefore holds by construction. It carries no regime information. Under the calls-positive/puts-negative convention printed in 04_Experimental_setup.tex:15, the same dates have 93 negative days, 75 below -$2B and mean +$1.26B (PostgreSQL post-rebuild, reproduced). Drop or heavily qualify 'persistent negative gamma regime driven by 0DTE' (05_Results.tex:161,180,182; 06_Discussion; 07_Conclusion; journal 05_Results.tex:190, 06_Discussion.tex:19).

claims.claim: (b) The 13-date raw-chain test (92.3% vs 61.5%) fed its GEX arm the same scalar (-$25.1B to -$38.8B); signed net on those dates differs.
claims.evidence: The 13 dates are the custom_ids in reports/validation/paper1_raw_chain/batch_raw_chain_20251125_153842.jsonl. In the unbiased gamma_positioning YAML their net_gex_usd runs from -25.13B (2024-01-19) to -38.83B (2024-01-17); the values are -32.49, -35.61, -38.83, -38.32, -25.13, -37.61, -36.22, -37.79, -29.29, -27.84, -28.73, -26.66, -25.49. The baseline detected count is 8/13 (8 detected with confidence 80-85; 5 not detected, confidence 0 on 01-09, 06-05, 06-07, 06-21, 06-28) = 61.5%. The raw-chain count of 12/13 and 'only 2024-01-02 missed (55)' are in RESULTS_SUMMARY.txt. I did not re-run the LLM. The prompt text of the baseline arm is not archived; that the agent was shown this value is inferred from the YAML gex_metrics plus src/agents/market_mechanics*.py, which prints 'Total GEX: $...' from gex_metrics. PostgreSQL signed net on the same 13 dates: negative on 7, below -$2B on 5, range -15.35B (2024-03-15) to +14.88B (2024-01-19). My independent recompute from the sqlite raw table gave 6 negative, 5 below -$2B, range -13.5 to +14.7. Extra finding on the design: the 13 dates are 8 'high' (detected, confidence >= 80) plus 5 'low' (not detected) baseline days, so the 61.5% baseline rate is partly set by how the dates were chosen (selected on the baseline outcome). The full-year baseline detection is 168/242 = 69.4%, and 51/72 on the dates available. The default sampler in scripts/validation/paper1/01_validate_raw_options_chain.py (seed 42, 25+25) does not reproduce the 13, so the selection rule is undocumented.
claims.correction: State in 04B_Methodology_Validation.tex that the baseline arm was shown the -(call+put) ex-0DTE scalar (-$25.1B to -$38.8B on these 13 dates), which is the same on every date and therefore not informative about regime, and that the 13 dates were stratified on baseline outcome (8 detections, 5 misses), so 61.5% is not an unbiased estimate of baseline detection (full-year 69.4%). With n=13 the 92.3% vs 61.5% difference is 12/13 vs 8/13. Soften 'GEX loses information' and 'directly refutes the pattern-matching critique' accordingly.
